newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo Q3 biggest sales in snack division.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo Q3 biggest sales in snack division.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc said Tuesday that worldwide beverage sales for the third quarter fell 1 percent to $2.8 billion, while worldwide snack food sales and profits rose 12 percent to $2.3 billion and $398 million, respectively. The company said worldwide restaurant sales were about even with prior year, but profits fell 9 percent primarily as a result of poor domestic results at Pizza Hut.

a) Included a benefit of $13 (Pizza Hut-$3, Taco Bell-$3, KFC-$2, International Restaurants-$3 and International Beverages-$2) in 1996 from lower depreciation and amortization expense resulting from the reduced carrying amount of certain long-lived assets due to the adoption of SFAS 121 as of the beginning of the fourth quarter of 1995.

b) Excluded a net gain of $22 in 1996 and a charge of ($3) in 1995 composed of a gain of $25 (Pizza Hut-$7, Taco Bell-$15, KFC-($1) and International Restaurants-$4) from sales of restaurants, including initial franchise fees, in excess of costs of closing other restaurants and unplanned spending of $3 to improve our Pizza Hut restaurant facilities in 1996 and, in 1995, a charge of ($3) (Pizza Hut-$(1) and KFC-($1) and Taco Bell ($1)) from store closure costs. Also excluded are the one-time international beverage impairment charges described in (c).

c) International beverage operating profit and equity(loss)/income included one-time charges of $157 and $233, respectively. The $57 is composed of charges related to impaired concentrate assets and the disposal of some non-core (primarily packaging) businesses. The $233 million is primarily composed of impaired investments in unconsolidated affiliates, primarily BAESA, and PepsiCo's 24% share of the one-time charges announced by BAESA on August 8, 1996.

d) Includes corporate headquarters expenses, minority interests, foreign exchange translation and transaction gains and losses and other items not allocated to the business segments. A net foreign exchange gain of $2 and loss of $9 were included in 1996 and 1995, respectively.
e) Included in Taco Bell's 1996 net sales was $38 from California Pizza Kitchen, which was consolidated by Taco Bell at the beginning of the third quarter of 1996.
